notices.title: Alberta opens its Budget 2027 survey
notices.summary: Albertans can share which services and investments they want the province to prioritize. The survey runs through January 4, 2027.

notices.title: Manitoba reports lower spending on agency nurses and aides
notices.summary: The province says spending on nursing and health-care aide agencies fell from $169.1 million to $122.6 million in 2025–26.

notices.title: Nunavut warns residents about phone scams
notices.summary: Consumer Affairs asks residents to be cautious when callers request personal or financial information. The alert explains how to handle suspicious calls and report fraud.

notices.title: Canada’s inflation rate held at 3.1% in October
notices.summary: Statistics Canada reports that consumer prices rose 3.1% from a year earlier, the same pace as September. Seasonally adjusted prices rose 0.2% from September.

notices.title: Ottawa dépose des mesures sur le logement et le coût de la vie
notices.summary: Les mesures proposées visent à favoriser la construction de logements et l’accession à la propriété. Elles prévoient aussi un supplément ponctuel à l’Allocation canadienne pour l’épicerie et les besoins essentiels.

notices.title: Funding intake opens for Inuit pre-employment training in Nunavut
notices.summary: CanNor is accepting expressions of interest for projects that prepare Inuit for federal public service work. It gives priority to Nunavut-based and Inuit-led organizations. The intake closes December 7 at 11:59 p.m. Yukon time.

notices.title: Canada selected to host the 2028 Francophonie Summit
notices.summary: Canada was named the host country at the 2026 summit. The event brings together members of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie.

notices.title: Le budget fédéral propose 1,5 milliard pour les patinoires et les loisirs
notices.summary: La proposition sur neuf ans réserve 750 millions de dollars aux patinoires et 750 millions à d’autres installations récréatives communautaires au Canada.

notices.title: Nova Scotia issues winter driving guidance
notices.summary: The province advises drivers to clear snow and ice, allow extra travel time and give snowplows room to work. The release links to road and weather information.

notices.title: Newfoundland and Labrador is hiring heavy equipment technicians
notices.summary: Transportation and Infrastructure is hiring at multiple locations for work on equipment such as trucks, graders and snowplows. The posting lists $27.61–$30.67 per hour and has no stated closing date.

notices.title: New Brunswick releases its second-quarter fiscal update
notices.summary: The province projects a $1.31-billion deficit for 2026–27, down $347 million from its previous forecast. The release explains what changed in revenue and spending.

notices.title: Saint John pulp mill air approval enters public review
notices.summary: New Brunswick has opened a 180-day public participation process on renewing the air quality approval for the Reversing Falls mill. The current approval expires May 31, 2027.

notices.title: P.E.I. seeks input on school codes of conduct
notices.summary: Islanders can comment on new codes of conduct for English- and French-language Island schools. Submissions are due December 12.

notices.title: Newfoundland and Labrador seeks input on rural revitalization
notices.summary: Residents, businesses and community groups can help shape the provincial strategy. The advisory lists in-person sessions through November 20 and explains other ways to take part.

notices.title: B.C. opens winter shelter spaces in 63 communities
notices.summary: BC Housing lists 6,588 shelter spaces across the province. The release links to help finding a place to stay.

notices.title: Saskatchewan awards bursaries to 57 young entrepreneurs
notices.summary: Business owners from 48 communities will receive $5,000 each through the Young Entrepreneur Bursary.

notices.title: Yukon announces more than $23 million in school investments
notices.summary: The territorial government announced funding to support students and school staff. The release breaks down where the money will go.

notices.title: Peterborough to receive up to $39.9 million for housing infrastructure
notices.summary: Ontario and Canada announced the funding after Peterborough committed to halving development charges for all housing types through March 31, 2029.

notices.title: N.W.T. invites feedback on its 2026 environment report
notices.summary: Residents can review territorial trends covering water, wildlife, climate and permafrost and share feedback until February 8, 2027.
